8:["$","$L13",null,{"data":{"chapterId":17,"verseId":21,"chapterTitle":"Examination of Action and Fruit","totalVerses":33,"verseData":{"id":"v17_21","number":21,"title":"Emptiness IS What Makes Karma Nonexpiring","sanskrit":{"text":"","transliteration":"","translation":"Because action does not arise, It is seen to be without essence. Because it is not arisen, It follows that it is nonexpiring."},"philosophy":{"insight":"The KEY logical move: action doesn't arise inherently → it lacks essence → BECAUSE it lacks essence, it is nonexpiring. Emptiness ENABLES persistence. This is the philosophical proof of v.20's thesis: emptiness = nonannihilation.","madhyamaka":"Anutpāda (non-arising) → niḥsvabhāva (without essence) → avipraṇāśa (nonexpiring). The logic: if action arose inherently, it would have svabhāva (essence). Having svabhāva means having inherent arising AND inherent cessation. But action lacks inherent arising, therefore lacks svabhāva, therefore lacks inherent cessation — making it conventionally nonexpiring.","quantum":"Virtual particles: they don't \"arise\" in the classical sense (off-shell, violating energy-momentum relations temporarily) yet mediate real forces (nonexpiring influence). Like karma: not inherently arisen, yet conventionally effective.","bridge":"Both virtual particles and karma function WITHOUT classical \"arising.\" Virtual particles: off-shell (not classically arisen) yet mediate real forces. Karma: not inherently arisen yet produces real consequences. Both: effectiveness doesn't require classical/inherent existence.","accessible":"Actions don't have a fixed, permanent core. BECAUSE they lack this rigid nature, their effects can persist flexibly through the flow of dependent arising. It's like water: because it has no fixed shape (no essence), it can flow continuously (nonexpiring). If it were solid ice (inherent essence), it would be stuck in one form.","twoTruths":"Ultimately: action does not arise (lacks inherent existence). Conventionally: action is nonexpiring (its potential persists). The connection: BECAUSE of the ultimate truth (emptiness), the conventional truth (nonexpiring karma) is possible. Emptiness enables conventional functioning.","commonMisconception":"NOT a contradiction (non-arising yet nonexpiring). These operate at different levels: non-arising = ultimate (no inherent existence). Nonexpiring = conventional (potential persists). If action doesn't arise inherently (it arises dependently), it lacks the svabhāva that would accompany inherent arising. Because the wave has no independent nature (no essence), it doesn't rigidly start and stop. It flows into other waves (nonexpiring influence)."},{"q":"Why does lacking essence make it nonexpiring?","a":"If action HAD essence, it would have an inherent \"expiration date\" — a fixed, determined cessation built into its nature. WITHOUT essence, there's no built-in cessation. Action can persist conventionally through dependent arising without hitting an inherent wall of cessation.","realLifeExample":"A rigid appointment (inherent) expires at its set time. An ongoing relationship (no fixed essence) continues indefinitely, adapting and persisting without a preset end date. Emptiness removes the \"expiration date.\""},{"q":"Isn't \"not arisen yet nonexpiring\" a contradiction?","a":"No — they operate at different levels. \"Not arisen\" = ultimate (no inherent existence). \"Nonexpiring\" = conventional (potential persists through dependent arising).
